body:
Source: GitHub issue #962, plus new evidence added as a comment on that issue during this session's release work. Re-verified on main @ b378c2a3.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package: packages/autopilot. The original issue quotes an ENOTEMPTY on `/tmp/ap-recover-*/repo/.git` from AC9 (`ac9_wallClockKillsFleet`, packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs:251-279) and hypothesizes the FAKE fleet child's process tree (packages/autopilot/test/helpers/fake-children.mjs) is still finishing when `fx.cleanup()` runs. Re-investigation this session found that hypothesis is very likely WRONG, or at best incomplete: `fake-children.mjs`'s `fakeSpawnImpl` (verified by reading it in full) is a pure in-process `EventEmitter`, never a real OS process — a "hung" fake child has no file descriptors, no subprocess, nothing that could hold `.git` open. It cannot itself cause an ENOTEMPTY.

What IS real: `packages/autopilot/test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs`'s `createFixture()` (used by AC9 via `createSequenceFixture`) builds THREE real git directories: `repo/` (working repo), `origin.git` (bare), and NET_GIT (`paths.netGit`, written by `packages/autopilot/lib/git-env.mjs`'s `writeNetGit`). recover-fixture.mjs lines 49-52 and 59-62 ALREADY set `gc.auto=0` and `gc.autoDetach=false` on `repo/` and `origin.git` specifically — with an inline comment citing the EXACT prior incident: "CI ENOTEMPTY flake, 2026-08-31: AC38 on the node-22 matrix job" / "ENOTEMPTY flake on the CI matrix, 2026-08-30". Confirmed via grep: THAT fix was never applied to NET_GIT. `writeNetGit` (packages/autopilot/lib/git-env.mjs:123-130) hand-writes NET_GIT's files directly (no `git init` call) and its `NET_GIT_CONFIG_TEMPLATE` (line 112-113) sets `core.repositoryformatversion`, `core.bare`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.hooksPath`, and the `origin` remote URLs — no `gc` section at all. `writeNetGit` is called from BOTH test fixtures (recover-fixture.mjs, preflight-world.mjs, preflight-ctx.mjs, review-ctx.mjs) AND production code (packages/autopilot/lib/init.mjs) — confirmed via `grep -rl writeNetGit packages/autopilot/`.

NET_GIT receives real pushes through it during network-git operations (`ctx.git.net`, packages/autopilot/lib/git-env.mjs's `netGitArgv`) — each push writes new loose objects into NET_GIT's OWN object store (the `objects/info/alternates` file lets it READ the primary repo's objects, but a push's OWN objects land in NET_GIT itself), so NET_GIT can accumulate enough loose objects to trigger `git gc --auto` exactly the same way `origin.git` did before its own fix.

SEPARATE NEW EVIDENCE (the cross-test-contamination angle, from this session's comment on #962): a DIFFERENT CI run showed the identical `"no run record for issue 7"` unhandledRejection — sourced from `packages/autopilot/lib/records.mjs:71`'s `update()` via `continueRun` (packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs:144) — surfacing as a FAILURE inside AC121 (packages/autopilot/test/spec-coverage.test.mjs:289), a completely unrelated test later in the same process. This is consistent with (not necessarily caused by) a background gc process from an EARLIER test's NET_GIT still writing/erroring when a LATER, unrelated test's async work touches overlapping state — but may also be a genuinely separate leak in the fleet-fake-kill path itself. Both are real, both need the reproduction loop to distinguish.

Tests: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs packages/autopilot/test/git-env.test.mjs` from the worktree root.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. Add `gc.auto=0` and `gc.autoDetach=false` to `NET_GIT_CONFIG_TEMPLATE` in packages/autopilot/lib/git-env.mjs (a `[gc]` section alongside the existing `[core]`/`[remote "origin"]` sections) — this is a PRODUCTION fix (writeNetGit is called from packages/autopilot/lib/init.mjs, not just test fixtures), matching the exact mitigation already applied to `repo/` and `origin.git` in recover-fixture.mjs for the identical symptom.
2. Reproduce AC9 (and ideally the whole run.test.mjs + spec-coverage.test.mjs pair) in a tight loop BEFORE and AFTER the fix — `for i in $(seq 1 50); do node --test packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs packages/autopilot/test/spec-coverage.test.mjs || break; done` or similar — to build real confidence the NET_GIT hypothesis actually explains the flake, since CI cannot directly verify a flake's absence. If the loop still reproduces ENOTEMPTY or the cross-test unhandledRejection after the NET_GIT fix, root-cause the REMAINING mechanism (the original fake-child-process-tree hypothesis is very likely a dead end per the evidence above — do not re-pursue it without new evidence; instead look at whether the fleet-fake-kill path's `continueRun` call itself is unawaited/fire-and-forget somewhere in packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs, which would be a genuine second, independent bug).
3. If a second, independent leak in the kill-timeout path is confirmed (not just the NET_GIT git-gc race), fix it at its source — e.g. ensure the code path that handles a killed fleet child's timeout genuinely awaits any in-flight `continueRun`/record-update work before the surrounding test can return and its fixture can clean up — rather than papering over the symptom with a longer timeout or a try/catch around the unhandledRejection.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `NET_GIT_CONFIG_TEMPLATE`'s output includes `gc.auto = 0` and `gc.autoDetach = false`. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/git-env.test.mjs` — add a new test asserting the template string (or a real `git config --file <NET_GIT config> --get gc.auto` read after `writeNetGit` runs) reflects both settings; do not merely assert the template STRING contains the substring "gc.auto" without a real config-read style check, since a hollow string-match test would not catch a typo'd key name.
- AC2 AC9 (`ac9_wallClockKillsFleet`) and the surrounding run.test.mjs suite pass repeatedly under a tight local loop (documented in the PR body: how many iterations, what was observed before/after). verify: manual loop, not a single `node --test` invocation (a single green run proves nothing about a flake).
- AC3 Existing suite green. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs packages/autopilot/test/git-env.test.mjs packages/autopilot/test/spec-coverage.test.mjs`
- AC4 Full package suite green. verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs autopilot` (or `node --test packages/autopilot/test/*.test.mjs` if unavailable)
- AC5 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: packages/fleet's own, separate ENOTEMPTY flake (issue #981, a different lane, different package, same general bug CLASS but an unrelated fixture). packages/autopilot/test/helpers/fake-children.mjs — re-verified above to be pure in-process, not a plausible root cause; do not restructure it speculatively. Any change to `packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs`'s kill/timeout logic UNLESS the loop-reproduction in NORMATIVE #2 proves the NET_GIT fix alone is insufficient — do not preemptively rewrite the async kill path on theory alone.
title: autopilot: NET_GIT never got the gc.auto=0 fix its sibling git dirs already have — root cause of AC9's ENOTEMPTY + cross-test unhandledRejection
